Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, the replacement for Gemini 3.8 Flash.
Google says it finishes tasks 2.5 times faster and already powers Google Search for everyone, for free.
Free Gemini app users get it automatically when a prompt calls for it.

threads_text: Google just swapped Gemini 3.8 Flash for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, and it already runs Google Search for everyone. Google says it is 2.5 times faster and makes over 5 times fewer made up claims, though those are Google's own numbers. Do you trust AI answers in Search more than you did a year ago?

paragraphs.text: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, 2026, a faster model in the Gemini 4 family that takes over from Gemini 3.8 Flash. According to VentureBeat and Digital Trends, the model is rolling out at once across Google Search, the Gemini app, Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and Google's business products.

Digital Trends reported that Google describes Hydrogen as its daily driver for agent work, built for speed and efficiency, while the heavier Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon models handle long, deep reasoning. Hydrogen arrives a few weeks after those two models.

Hydrogen now powers Google Search for all users worldwide, according to Digital Trends and Chrome Unboxed, and MakeUseOf noted that it is free to use there. Google says the model understands multi-part questions, typos and very specific requests better, gives answers that are easier to scan and shows a wider range of links in results.

In the Gemini app, Hydrogen appears in the model picker. Free users are routed to it automatically when the app judges that a prompt calls for it. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers also get it in Google Sheets, where Google says financial models are built more than 30 percent faster, and in the Antigravity coding tool.

Developers can use it in Google AI Studio, Android Studio and the Gemini API, and Google Cloud lists the model as generally available, according to VentureBeat. The context window is about 1 million tokens, and the model accepts text, images, audio and video as input.

Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times as fast as Gemini 3.8 Flash. At its default high reasoning setting, it scored 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, VentureBeat reported, compared with 31 for Flash and one point above Gemini 4 Argon. At the new xhigh setting it reached 54.

On Terminal-Bench 4.1, Google's own comparison shows Hydrogen completing 57 percent of tasks, against 18.2 percent for Flash and 63.9 percent for Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5. Digital Trends reported that Google places Hydrogen ahead of OpenAI's GPT 6.1 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5.5 on knowledge tests, but slightly behind in science, math and computer use.

Google also made safety claims. According to Digital Trends and MakeUseOf, the company says Hydrogen makes more than five times fewer fabricated claims than Flash, reduces overreach in agent tasks by up to 81 percent and is up to twice as unlikely to get around permission limits when a task is blocked. These figures come from Google and have not been checked independently.

The standard API price is $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, including reasoning tokens. VentureBeat reported that this matches the standard Flash pricing scheduled from January 1, 2027, and is twice the introductory Flash rate that runs through December 31, 2026. Batch and Flex requests cost half the standard rate.

Box, which tested the model early, reported that accuracy on its complex work evaluation rose from 74 percent with Flash to 79 percent with Hydrogen, VentureBeat said, with tasks taking less than half as long.

For most people the change is invisible but large: the model answering their Google searches has been replaced without any action on their part. The higher developer price suggests Google is betting that speed and fewer errors matter more to businesses than the cheapest possible rate.
The next thing to watch is whether independent testers confirm Google's claims about fewer fabricated answers, since Hydrogen now writes the AI answers in Google Search for all users.
